title: Chicken pot pie
subtitle: American pastry-topped chicken-and-vegetable pot pie
excerpt: Tender chunks of chicken, carrot, peas, and celery in a rich cream-and-stock sauce, topped with a butter shortcrust or puff pastry lid and baked until golden. The definitive American comfort food pie.
sourceNotes: Chicken pot pie appears in Fannie Farmer's The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896, public domain) and in Joy of Cooking (1931). The deep-dish, single-crust version with a cream-based filling is the standard American form documented throughout twentieth-century American cookbooks.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble before baking and freeze. Bake from frozen at 180°C for 60 to 70 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made the day before and refrigerated. Assemble and bake just before serving.

content.text: Chicken pot pie is a two-stage operation: you make the filling, you make the pastry, you assemble and bake. Using good chicken stock for the sauce is what separates a good pot pie from a mediocre one. The vegetables should be slightly undercooked when they go into the pie, as they continue cooking in the oven.

items.prepNote: or boneless thigh; poached in stock and shredded or cut into chunks

content.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until softened. Add the flour and stir into a paste. Cook for 2 minutes. Gradually add the hot stock, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes until thickened. Add the cream and thyme. Season generously.
Add the chicken and frozen peas. Stir to combine. Taste and adjust the seasoning. The filling should be thick enough to hold its shape; it will loosen slightly in the oven. Leave to cool slightly.

Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Pour the filling into a large, deep baking dish. Roll the pastry to fit the top of the dish with a 2 cm overhang. Lay it over the filling, pressing the edges to the rim of the dish. Brush with beaten egg. Cut a few steam holes in the top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden brown and the filling is bubbling through the steam holes. Leave to rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Pastry is soggy on the bottom
items.cause: Filling was too hot when the pastry went on, or no steam holes cut
items.fix: Let the filling cool slightly before topping with pastry. Cut steam holes in the pastry lid to allow steam to escape.

items.symptom: Filling is too thin when the pie is cut
items.cause: Not reduced enough in the sauce stage
items.fix: The sauce should be thick before the pie goes in the oven. It should coat a spoon heavily.

content.text: Chicken pot pie is New England winter food that spread across the United States during the twentieth century. It became an American institution in two forms: home-cooked and frozen. Swanson introduced the frozen chicken pot pie in 1951 and sold millions of units a year. The homemade version outperforms the frozen by every measure. It is one of the most satisfying things to pull from an oven on a cold Sunday evening.
